thread.title: Amazon extends streak of not buying back its stock to 6 years

author: Tomi Kilgore
title: Amazon extends streak of not buying back its stock to 6 years
text: Amazon.com Inc. AMZN, +4.20% disclosed in its first-quarter quarter earnings filing that it continued to choose not to buy back its shares, to extend the streak of not repurchasing stock to 24 quarters, or 6 years. The technology giant as a $5 billion buyback program in place, since February 2016, with no fixed expiration But the lack of repurchases hasn't hurt the stock price, as Amazon shares soared 23.8% during the quarter, compared with a 1.2% decline in the S&P 500 SPX, +0.12% The last time Amazon repurchased shares was the first quarter of 2012, when it paid $960 million to buy back 5.3 million shares, filings show. With the stock up 4.8% in midday trade after blowout first-quarter results , Amazon is now the 2nd-biggest U.S. company by market capitalization at $771.6 billion, behind Apple Inc.'s AAPL, -1.04% $822.4 billion market cap. Filings show Apple spent about $29 billion on buying back its stock in 2017, and the stock rose 46.1% last year, while Amazon shares climbed 56.0%.
